title: Introduce slew-rate-aware canary throttler to smooth traffic adjustments
author: Ava Martinez
description: Add a slew-rate-aware throttler into the canary evaluation pipeline to prevent noisy transient traffic spikes from triggering aggressive rollout changes. Motivation: we observed several incidents where sudden upstream traffic bursts caused the canary evaluator to overreact, rapidly shifting traffic weights and creating oscillations that hurt tail latency and customer experience. This PR implements a compact time-derivative metric (request_rate_slew) and a configurable smoothing/throttling policy that gates traffic weight updates when the instantaneous slew exceeds a safety threshold. The implementation is conservative by default, exposes runtime knobs (window_ms, slew_threshold, max_step_pct, cooldown_ms) and integrates with existing rollout guards so that canaries only change weight if both quality metrics and slew constraints are satisfied. Included are unit tests, a synthetic e2e job that reproduces the original oscillation, dashboard panels, and alerts for sustained-high-slew conditions. Also added docs outlining recommended thresholds for common traffic shapes and an opt-out flag for legacy canary behaviors.
